description:
A package tree assembles and publishes on Windows, and a manifest a test authors parses on the host that wrote it.

## Background

Two independent defects fail the offline profile-adoption job on Windows.

Publishing an assembled package tree reports "filesystem operation required for durable transactions is unsupported: atomic no-replace directory publication". The publication renames a staged directory onto an unoccupied destination through a capability-anchored no-replace rename, and refusing rather than overwriting an occupied destination is the property it exists to hold (`@/inv/atomic-writes`). The underlying rename reports the operation as unsupported on Windows, so staging the repository's own packages fails before any test using them runs. Windows does offer a no-replace directory rename, so the refusal reflects a missing platform path rather than a platform without the guarantee.

Separately, a helper that writes a manifest declaring an asset composes the asset's target with the host's path separator and writes the result into a TOML basic string. On Windows the separator is a backslash, so the value becomes an invalid escape sequence and the manifest the helper just wrote does not parse: the reported error names an unexpected escape and quotes the line. The declaration is meant to carry a repository-relative path, which is separator-independent by definition.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Publishing a staged package tree at an unoccupied destination succeeds on Windows.
- [hard] REQ-02: Publishing at an occupied destination is still refused rather than overwritten, on every platform.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test manifest declares repository-relative target paths that parse as written, whatever separator the host uses.
- [hard] REQ-04: The paths a test helper composes for a manifest are separator-independent by construction, rather than corrected at each call site.
- [hard] REQ-05: Every profile-adoption acceptance test whose failure was either defect passes on Windows.


## Resolution

Windows support is out of scope for the container that surfaced this: the workflow's Windows leg is removed rather than repaired, so no job observes the defect. The diagnosis above is retained for whoever restores that platform.
title: Assemble and publish a package tree on Windows
